blockers:
- BLOCKING (behavior): the dev-server skill's stop path contradicts the Worker.operations role. packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/skills/dev-server/SKILL.md lines 'Stop it' (and step 2, 'stops no process it did not start') have the root dispatch a new Worker.operations Assignment to kill the process id recorded by an earlier Assignment. packages/runtime/src/instructions/claude-5.5/roles/worker-operations/dev-server.md (unchanged from the base and now in every worker-operations agent) says 'Stop only a process this Assignment started, and only when the root says so.' The start Assignment and the stop Assignment are different Assignments, so a compliant Worker.operations must refuse the stop and the shared server leaks with its port held. The same role text lets it 'reuse a healthy one' it finds by process, port or URL, so it can record a pid for a server it did not start. The skill says a server another person started is left running, so the two texts disagree on that case. Why it blocks: the requested dev-server lifecycle (start, share, stop) is not workable as written. The fix is a wording change: let the role stop a process whose recorded pid the root names, provided it was started for this work and not reused from a foreign server. The R-DEVSERVER test only checks phrase presence, so it will not catch this.
notes:
- Non-blocking, optional. The skill assumes a background job started by a one-shot Worker.operations survives that subagent's end. I could only read this, not run it. If the harness reaps it, Worker.visual and Reviewer.visual find the URL dead and report blocked. The skill offers no fallback beyond 'restart it'.
- Non-blocking, optional. The embedded frontend-design body keeps its own H1 ('# Frontend Design') and H2 sections under the role's '## Design guidance'. That puts an H1 in the middle of the agent prompt, beside '# Specialist conduct', and the body includes a 'Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique' section and 'confirm with the client'. Both read oddly for background agents that cannot ask questions, and for Reviewer.visual, who builds nothing.
- Non-blocking, optional. frontendDesign() in packages/integrations/claude/src/agents.ts splits on /^---$/m and assumes LF line endings and one frontmatter block. The test only checks from '# Frontend Design' onward with length > 5000. A vendored update that adds preamble text before the heading would be dropped without failing the build.
- Non-blocking, optional. Duplicated text: the blocking-rubric sentence in root/assignments.md copies merge-ready.md, and the 'material discrepancy' list sits in root/visual.md, specialist/interface-inspection.md and requirements.md. Nothing ties them together, so they can drift. The copying is deliberate, because the root has no merge-ready section and the specialists need the full rubric.
- Non-blocking, optional. inspectionTools() still derives tool grants by regex from prose. Moving the text out of a skill makes the prose the live permission list for both visual agents. Net effect of this change: html_render is no longer granted to Worker.visual or Reviewer.visual (confirmed in the dist tools lines). It is still granted to the root, so this looks intended. preview_evaluate is still granted because the prose names it; that was already the case on the base.
- Non-blocking, optional. Prompt weight rises: merge-ready, the inspection rules and about 5k characters of design guidance are now in every dispatch of the roles that carry them (worker-visual, reviewer-visual and the code roles). This is the deliberate trade the user asked for.
- The license ships once at dist/licenses/frontend-design/LICENSE.txt, and both visual role sections name the path. The vendored SKILL.md and LICENSE.txt are unchanged under vendor/. The embedded body drops only the frontmatter. This is acceptable.
- Out of scope as the Assignment stated, listed only as a note: docs/attributions.md, docs/development.md, docs/usage.md and docs/decisions.md still name the removed skills. Also docs/pi/claude-parity.md (lines 49, 88, 92, 117-119, 128) still describes merge-ready and interface-inspection as skills preloaded by seven roles, and frontend-design as a vendored skill.
- The commit includes 5 .holyagent assignment JSON files. Earlier commits on the branch do the same, so it is the branch's pattern and not scope noise.
- Generator correctness, read from the diff and confirmed by the passing tests. Each CONDITIONAL_SECTIONS entry reaches exactly its roles. Order is role sections, then conduct, then writing bar, merge-ready and inspection. frontend-design is appended after its framing section only in worker-visual and reviewer-visual. The tests assert one copy in the right roles and zero elsewhere, and no preloaded skills. dist/skills now holds only dev-server and user-busy, with no stale files. git status in the worktree is clean. I did not run mise run build separately. The 'generated plugin is in step with its sources' test in the verify run covers dist against a fresh build.
